tasks.q: What is John von Neumann best known for in computing?
a: Describing a computer design where programs are stored in memory
tasks.fb: His 1945 report described the stored-program computer.

tasks.q: When did von Neumann describe his architecture?
tasks.fb: Around the end of the Second World War.

tasks.q: In von Neumann architecture, where are instructions stored?
a: In main memory, together with the data
In a separate memory from data
On paper tape outside the computer
tasks.fb: Storing both in the same memory is the key feature.

tasks.q: Why is the stored-program idea so useful?
a: The same computer can run different programs just by loading them into memory
It makes computers use no power
It removes the need for a CPU
tasks.fb: Early computers had to be rewired for each new job.

tasks.q: What does the program counter hold?
a: The address of the next instruction
The result of the last calculation

tasks.q: Which register holds the results of calculations?
tasks.fb: The ALU's results go into the accumulator.

tasks.q: Which register holds the address of data to be fetched from memory?

a: Data or an instruction fetched from memory, or waiting to be written to memory
The address of the next instruction
tasks.fb: It's the CPU's 'in tray and out tray' for memory.

tasks.q: What is the main difference in Harvard architecture?
a: Instructions and data are held in separate memories
It stores everything on a hard drive
It only works with the internet
tasks.fb: Separate memories mean both can be fetched at once.

tasks.q: Where is Harvard architecture commonly used?
tasks.fb: Many small dedicated devices use it.

tasks.q: Which of these is a Python keyword?
tasks.fb: while starts a loop. The others are just names a programmer might choose.

tasks.q: Why can't you call a variable 'if'?
a: It's a keyword with a special meaning in the language
Variables must start with a capital letter
It would use too much memory
tasks.fb: Keywords are reserved by the language.

tasks.q: Match each component or register to its definition.
pairs: Stores the address of the next instruction; increments each cycle
Decodes instructions and sends control signals
Stores the address of the data to be fetched or stored
Performs mathematical calculations and logical operations
Stores data fetched from, or to be written to, memory
Fast memory for frequently used instructions and data

info.title: A brilliant mind
info.text: Von Neumann also made major contributions to maths, physics and game theory, and worked on some of the first electronic computers.

info.title: Rewiring computers
info.text: Before stored programs, machines like ENIAC had to be physically rewired with cables to change the job they did.

info.title: The von Neumann bottleneck
info.text: Because instructions and data share one memory, the CPU can only fetch one at a time. This limit is called the von Neumann bottleneck.

info.title: Best of both
info.text: Modern CPUs mix both ideas: they use von Neumann-style shared RAM, but separate caches for instructions and data, like Harvard architecture.

info.title: Harvard Mark I
info.text: Harvard architecture is named after the Harvard Mark I computer of 1944, which read instructions from punched tape and kept data separately.

info.title: How many keywords?
info.text: Python has about 35 keywords. Try typing help("keywords") into Python to see the full list.
